items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: She was also going to see a woman who was trying to book musicians, named Marianne Knüppel.

ctx.x: The band was not too bad considering that Donald Brown had never played drums before and Lude had not rehearsed with us. The front line was very nice together, and the public enjoyed our music which was our main interest, and after I got my voice back, everything was fine.

The job at the Esquire-Hungaria was a break-in for the orchestra, but we needed an engagement for the month of July to keep us going until August. So Lily decided to go to Germany and try to find an engagement. I was not too hot about her going there alone, but she could speak German and we had the address - a booking agency in Hamburg. She was also going to see a woman who was trying to book musicians, named Marianne Knüppel. I also wrote to my friend Hans Bluthner in Berlin and told him that Lily would be…

A few days after Lily left, a telegramme came to the pension where we were staying, announcing the death of Lily's mother, and this really upset me. The telegramme had been sent first to the American Express in Paris, then sent in Zurich in an envelope, and it would be too late for Lily to attend the funeral. I telephoned to Hans in Berlin, but Lily had already been in Berlin and left for Hamburg.
